questions: During these episodes, do symptoms worsen with repeated use (e.g., speaking or looking up) and improve with rest?
During these episodes, do you have double vision (new or worsening), and does it improve after resting for a few minutes?
During an episode, have you noticed weakness in your arms, legs, or trouble holding your head up that gets worse with repeated use and improves after rest?
During an episode, do you have trouble breathing or a change in voice/swallowing (e.g., choking, drooling, or being unable to speak full sentences) that improves after resting?
During these episodes, do your eyelids droop (ptosis) more noticeably after holding your eyes open for 30–60 seconds, and does it improve after resting?
answers: Yes, it tends to get worse during the episode when I try to talk or sometimes when I’m looking around. When I can rest and calm down, it usually eases up a bit.
I don’t have double vision that I’m aware of. But my eyelids feel really hard to open or lift during the episodes, and after a few minutes of resting it can get a little better.

I’ve mainly had muscle spasms and stiffness in my face and neck, and it makes it hard to turn my head to one side and even keep my jaw open. I don’t notice true arm or leg weakness, and it doesn’t really change with repeated use—more like it comes and goes, and rest helps a bit.

Yes. I feel like I can’t breathe well during the episode, and my tongue feels hard to keep in my mouth—so I have trouble speaking and it’s uncomfortable. Rest helps it ease somewhat after a few minutes.
Yes, my eyelids are hard to open or lift, like they won’t stay up. If I keep them open for a bit, it gets worse, and then after I rest it improves a little.
